title: Monsters: Ippyaku Sanjou Hiryuu Jigoku
content:
Imagine going back in time and tapping young Oda on the shoulder, informing him that in a little bit shy of three decades, one of his one-shots, Monsters, should get a high budget Anime adaptation that stands tall next to his timeless masterpiece, One Piece, a behemoth of a Manga that he will be working on for the rest of his life. He would laugh it off and tell you “God damn right” because that’s who m goat is.

I’m sure my intro made no sense, but that’s also how little it matters to have to be a big One Piece fan before you can enjoy this ONA release to its fullest.

Yeah sure, it has canon ties with One Piece, something Oda has been laying down the foundation for, for decades at this point, but don’t left that shy you from absolutely enjoying this as a standalone story with its own charm and pull.

You if the biggest discussions around the release of the ONA were about the art direction they are gonna take. Is it One Piece like? Dragon-Ball Broly like? Turned out it was a mix of those and more. They really nailed the vibes that the art stye carried with its washed out colors, pastel hues and faint point strokes. It really felt like peeking at a scrible on one of Oda’s sketchbooks. Afterthought dools he had on a pile around his trash bin. Only, that nothing about this was trash, no is anything inside Oda’s working room.

One thing that really caught me off guard was the OST and voice acting. It felt so refreshing not having to deal with Toei’s 90s SFX catalog for once.

I don’t know how to feel abou the characters themselves though. One thing for sure, the character design carries all the weight there. Other than that, it was a showcase of a by-the-book Shounen cast brought nothing too memorable with them.

Overall: 7.54/10.
